subject: Next steps: PoC & deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T16:15:00Z
Subject: Recap & proposed PoC plan \u0014 deployment mode options

Hi Lindsey \u0014

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed PoC/trial plan so we can align on the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Call recap:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood for latency-sensitive customer-facing features and reduce per-token cost while maintaining output quality.
- Primary constraints: data residency in US, production latency target < 200ms 95th pctl, and E2E throughput for peak 100 RPS.
- Stakeholders on your side: Product (you), ML infra, and Procurement (you mentioned looping them in).

Deployment mode considerations (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, no infra lift. Good if no strict VPC or on-prem requirement.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and better unit economics at scale; requires contract/commit.
- Private VPC / On-prem: for regulated data residency or strict network isolation \u0014 longer lead time for networking & onboarding.

Proposed PoC/trial plan (60 days target):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & access \u0014 confirm data residency and test account type (Hosted trial vs Dedicated eval). I attached a short SOW for scope.
2) Week 1-2: Integration & baseline \u0014 send representative traffic, run baseline perf/latency tests.
3) Week 3-4: Workload tuning \u0014 batching, kv-cache config, and basic quantization recommendations.
4) Week 5-7: Evaluate quality & cost \u0014 run production-like queries and measure token cost/latency tradeoffs.
5) Week 8: Review & recommendation \u0014 choose final deployment mode and next steps (commit for Dedicated or schedule Private on-boarding).

Success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency target: 95th pctl < 200ms on 90% of representative queries.
- Cost target: <= $0.015 per 1k tokens (goal to be refined during PoC).
- Functionality: end-to-end inference with prefix caching and tool calls passing QA prompts.

Attachments: PoC_SOW_v1.pdf, Deployment_Options_Comparison.xlsx (high-level pros/cons & rough TTM).

Next steps: can you confirm (a) whether you need Private VPC/on-prem for this PoC or whether Hosted/Dedicated is acceptable for the initial trial, (b) who from ML infra should be included, and (c) procurement contact? If Hosted/Dedicated is acceptable we can aim to start next week; Private will add ~3-6 weeks for network and security onboarding.

Thanks \u0014 happy to jump on a short 15-min sync to confirm.

Best,
Ben

Hi Lindsey / Procurement \u0014

Per our thread, attached is an updated PoC SOW (PoC_SOW_v1.pdf) with SOC2 audit contact and a short appendix on data residency controls for Hosted. High-level notes:

- Hosted API: US-only data residency option for PoC (logs and persisted outputs stored in our US region). This is generally sufficient for evaluation; retention and export controls included in the SOW appendix.
- Dedicated: recommended if you want predictable throughput and improved unit economics straight away; typical lead time is ~2-3 weeks after contract signature to reserve capacity. Minimum commit options are outlined in the SOW.
- Private VPC / On-prem: for strict network isolation \u0014 estimate 4-6 weeks to stand up networking and on-boarding depending on customer's firewall/peering schedule.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
1) Procurement: review attached SOW and the brief residency appendix. Please confirm any additional security artifact requests (we can provide SOC2 report and a security questionnaire response).
2) Decision point: choose Hosted (quick start) vs Dedicated (reserved) vs Private (longer runway) by next Wednesday 2027-05-12 to keep a 60-day PoC.
3) Kickoff: tentative kickoff week of 2027-05-17 if Hosted/Dedicated is selected.
